tasks.title: Bug 2: Corsair Vengeance RGB DDR4 RAM is not detected
tasks.body: User's PC: AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D, MSI B550-A PRO (MS-7C56) motherboard, Corsair Vengeance RGB DDR4 3200 MHz 64 GB (4 x 16 GB), 240 Hz monitor (Samsung Odyssey G40B) plus a second Acer XFA240, Windows 11. Other RGB software running: MSI Center / Mystic Light and SteelSeries GG / SteelSeries Engine. Central RGB currently detects only a Razer Huntsman V2 TKL and the MSI B550-A PRO, no RAM. Home shows only 1 RGB device and the four RAM sticks never appear.
tasks.assignment: Branch: test-ram-detect. Find out plainly why the Corsair Vengeance RGB DDR4 3200 sticks are missing. Check: which Corsair DDR4 RGB models OpenRGB supports and how they are detected (SMBus/I2C on AMD B550, piix4 bus); whether the OpenRGB version Central RGB uses needs PawnIO on Windows and whether Central RGB installs and starts it; whether OpenRGB/Central RGB run with admin rights; and whether MSI Mystic Light (MSI Center) or SteelSeries GG holding the SMBus blocks detection (Central RGB already warns that Mystic Light holds the motherboard and RAM lighting). Read rgb_engine.py, central_rgb.py (Devices page, the other-RGB-software warning) and central_rgb.iss. If it can be fixed in the app, fix it on this branch (for example: detect that RAM is blocked and tell the user exactly why and what to change, keep Mystic Light from grabbing the RAM after Close them, retry RAM detection once the bus is free) without restarting OpenRGB in a loop. Add a fake Corsair Vengeance RGB DDR4 device to tests/fake_openrgb.py and a test for the new behaviour. RULES FOR THIS TASK: Start from the latest main. Work only on the branch named above and push it to origin; do NOT open a pull request (PRs into main auto-merge). Commit as the user: git -c user.name="steven-t0764" -c user.email="323795143+steven-t0764@users.noreply.github.com" commit, and never add Co-Authored-By, Claude-Session, 'Generated with Claude Code' or any Claude/Anthropic line to commits. Keep the fan safety rules exactly as they are (fans never below 20%, pumps never below 70%, every fan 100% at 90 C CPU or GPU, closing the app hands fans back to the BIOS) and do not touch the DDR5 once-per-boot RAM guard (it lives on the test-ddr5 branch; leave it alone). Keep the GPL-3.0 header on every source file. Windows-only code must fail quietly elsewhere. Put any new test, fake device or helper script in tests/ and commit it. Before you finish: python -m py_compile every changed .py file and run python -m unittest discover tests; both must pass. In your result, write plain-English findings (cause, what you changed, what could not be verified without the real PC) and link the final commit as an immutable https://github.com/steven-t0764/CentralRGB/commit/<sha> link.

tasks.title: Settings: Dark / Light appearance toggle
tasks.body: Steven asked for a dark/light theme toggle on the Settings page. Today every theme in central_rgb.py THEMES is dark and ctk.set_appearance_mode('dark') is hard-coded.
tasks.assignment: Branch: feat-theme-toggle. Add an Appearance setting with two choices, Dark and Light, as a Windows 11-style row on the Settings page next to the existing theme dropdown (reuse the existing settings row helper). Save it as settings['appearance'] = 'dark' | 'light'; a missing or unknown value means dark, so older settings files load unchanged. Give every entry in THEMES (and the default gunmetal SOLID palette) a light variant: light BG/SIDE/CARD/CARD2/LINE/TEXT/MUTED/TRACK/HOVER/SEL/BTN values, keeping each theme's accent hue but darkened enough for readable contrast on light panels (aim for WCAG AA 4.5:1 for body text; use the existing readable-text helper for text on accent colours). Apply it through _apply_theme (e.g. _apply_theme(key, appearance)) and the existing live rebuild in _switch_theme, so flipping the toggle repaints the window in place with no restart and lighting, fans, sensors and OpenRGB keep running. Set ctk.set_appearance_mode to match, and make win_effects use a light title bar in light mode (failing quietly off Windows). Tests: add tests/test_appearance.py covering: default is dark when the key is missing; every theme has a complete light palette (all SOLID keys present, valid hex); body text vs card contrast is at least 4.5:1 in light mode for every theme; toggling through the harness rebuilds the Settings page without errors and persists the value. Add a light-mode option to tests/preview.py (e.g. --appearance light) and capture Home, Lighting, Fans, Monitor and Settings in light mode. RULES FOR THIS TASK: Follow CLAUDE.md. Start from the latest main and open a pull request into main from the branch named above; it merges itself once the windows check passes, so if windows fails read the log, fix it on the same branch and push again. Commit as the user: git -c user.name="steven-t0764" -c user.email="323795143+steven-t0764@users.noreply.github.com" commit, and never add Co-Authored-By, Claude-Session, 'Generated with Claude Code' or any Claude/Anthropic line to commits or the PR. Keep the fan safety rules exactly as they are (tests/test_fan_safety.py must keep passing) and do not touch the DDR5 once-per-boot RAM guard (test-ddr5 branch). Keep the GPL-3.0 header on every source file. Windows-only code must fail quietly elsewhere. Settings files from older versions must still load (a missing appearance key means dark). Do not restyle anything outside this task: the dark look of every existing theme must stay pixel-identical. Before pushing: python -m py_compile every changed .py and xvfb-run -a python -m unittest discover tests; both must pass. Same PR: a line under ## Unreleased in CHANGELOG.md, README.md (Settings section) and tests/README.md for any new test or preview script. Run tests/preview.py under Xvfb and attach or describe the screenshots in the PR.
